article: Run Windows PowerShell 5.1 from C++ through a C++/CLI DLL
findings: Narrowed the example to Windows PowerShell 5.1 on .NET Framework 4.7.2 or later; removed the incompatible blanket advice to use System.Management.Automation 5.x or 7.x and replaced it with Microsoft.PowerShell.5.ReferenceAssemblies 1.1.0.

Clarified that the caller enables /clr and is mixed-mode; both projects must match the .NET Framework target, build configuration, and x86/x64 architecture. Removed the hard-coded Debug DLL #using path in favor of the Visual Studio project reference.
Added deterministic PowerShell object disposal, checks for HadErrors and the error stream, and security guidance that AddScript executes code with the application's user permissions.

Explained that PowerShell 7 requires a separate matching .NET host or pwsh child process; fixed duplicate dates, preserved the 2025-04-16 publication date, added lastmod and localized descriptions, and cited Microsoft sources.
Compared the full Japanese article with all twelve translations, including all code blocks, setup, runtime constraints, security notes, summary structure, and references.
